1. Present appeal u/S 372 Cr.PC is filed by the complainant in FIR no. 299/2002, PS Shalimar Bagh,

However, after marriage the A1 and his family members started harassing the complainant and kept on demanding more and more dowry.
A1 used to beat the complainant in which his family member also used to join.
Complainant was taunted and tortured for bringing less dowry and attempts were made to eliminate the complainant.

9. Hon'ble Supreme Court has, on the legal position of the power of Appellate Court in dealing with judgments of acquittal, in Ghurey Lal Vs. State of U.P, (2008) 10 SCC 450, after going through previous judgments, has held that:-

entities.text: Ghurey Lal Vs. State of U.P, (2008) 10 SCC 450
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"72. The following principles emerge from the cases above:
1. The appellate court may review the evidence in appeals against acquittal under sections 378 and 386 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Its power of reviewing evidence is wide and the appellate court can reappreciate the entire evidence on record.
It can review the trial court's conclusion with respect to both facts and law.
2. The accused is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
The accused possessed this presumption when he was before the trial court.
The trial court's acquittal bolsters the presumption that he is innocent.
3. Due or proper weight and consideration must be given to the trial court's decision.
This is especially true when a witness' credibility is at issue.
It is not enough for the High Court to take a different view of the evidence.
There must also be substantial and compelling reasons for holding that trial court was wrong.

73. In light of the above, the High Court and other appellate courts should follow the well settled principles crystallized by number of judgments if it is going to overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal:
1. The appellate court may only overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal if it has "very substantial and compelling reasons" for doing so.

A number of instances arise in which the appellate court would have "very substantial and compelling reasons"
to discard the trial court's decision.

sentences.text: The complaint on which FIR is registered in itself is not a substantive piece of evidence.
It can only be used for corroboration of or for contradiction with its maker.
Therefore it is the testimony of the complainant only, which can be read against the accused persons.

11. The examination in chief of complainant, which runs in 9 pages, recorded on 4 different dates, do not specify any date or time when alleged cruelties were committed by the in laws before 13 July 1996.
For 13th July 1996 it is deposed by complainant that at about 10.15 pm she was asked by her in laws to prepare tea an she went to kitchen.
However, there was leakage of gas, therefore, she reported about it to in laws on which the husband i.e. A1 thrashed her.
This is the only incident of which some specification is provided in the trial.

The complainant had left her matrimonial house the next day i.e. 14 th July 1996 but from 14th July 1996 to 30th March 1997, when Panchayat was conducted, no step was taken from the side of complainant.
The first complaint before CAW cell as per the statement of complainant herself was filed in the month of October 1997 only after the A1 filed divorce petition in the month of July 1997.

sentences.text: 13. The prosecution has not explained the delay in filing the complaint.

Ld. Counsel for appellant would submit that the complainant was expecting settlement, therefore, she did not file the complaint however, that alone is not sufficient to not pursue her complaint after the divorce petition is filed.
14. The record produced by Pw7 shows that the first complaint of the complainant was received on 08.10.1997.
However, that original complaint or its copy are not proved by prosecution.
It appears that in complaint dated 08.10.1997 allegations of cheating were also involved.
This shows that the contents of complaint Ex.Pw1/B are different from the first complaint.
Hence Ex.Pw1/B cannot be treated as a reliable document to corroborate the complainant.
15. So far as charge under section 406 IPC is concerned it rests only with those properties which are exclusively owned by complainant, like the stridhan, in this case.
Any gift given in marriage to any family member of accused or for joint use of parties cannot become a property under trust.
It has to be the exclusive property of giver i.e. the complainant.
Complainant in her statement Ex.Pw1/C has not specified which stridhan was entrusted by her and with whom.
Merely because after failing of marriage the dowry articles were seized to be returned to complainant does not make them the property of trust.

Further there has to be a specific demand for return of the property which is given in trust or disposal of such property against the specific C.A. No. 77/2022 Vandana Dhaka Vs. State Page no. 10 of 11 VIKRAM Date: 2024.09.13 instruction.

However, that original complaint or its copy are not proved by prosecution.
It appears that in complaint dated 08.10.1997 allegations of cheating were also involved.
This shows that the contents of complaint Ex.Pw1/B are different from the first complaint.
Hence Ex.Pw1/B cannot be treated as a reliable document to corroborate the complainant.
15. So far as charge under section 406 IPC is concerned it rests only with those properties which are exclusively owned by complainant, like the stridhan, in this case.
Any gift given in marriage to any family member of accused or for joint use of parties cannot become a property under trust.
It has to be the exclusive property of giver i.e. the complainant.
Complainant in her statement Ex.Pw1/C has not specified which stridhan was entrusted by her and with whom.
Merely because after failing of marriage the dowry articles were seized to be returned to complainant does not make them the property of trust.
Further there has to be a specific demand for return of the property which is given in trust or disposal of such property against the specific C.A. No. 77/2022 Vandana Dhaka Vs. State Page no. 10 of 11 VIKRAM Date: 2024.09.13 instruction.
Nothing of such sort was alleged in the complaint not deposed by any witness.
